findings.reason: §8 should drop the IMAS arm from the bridge call (or state why it stays) rather than leave a second DD retrieval owner running on every escalated source under a cap that truncates the arm it keeps.
findings.text: `compute_semantic_matches` searches the `imas_node_embedding` arm itself (its docstring lists "1. imas_node_embedding (primary: target IMAS fields)") alongside the wiki and code arms; §8 calls it "the per-source bridge" that "supplies only each source's own wiki and code matches", but that narrowing is done by post-hoc filtering at imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:681–694 (`[m for m in matches if m.get("content_type") != "imas"]`), so the IMAS arm is still executed and discarded — the same DD retrieval `retrieve_candidates` owns in imas_codex/ids/candidates.py:120 — and because the call passes `k_per_source=20` across all three arms, discarded `imas` hits consume the cap and can truncate the wiki/code bridge the plan says it keeps. Every site of this one type: the IMAS arm in `compute_semantic_matches` (`imas_codex/ids/tools.py:769`, owner to extend: `retrieve_candidates`, `imas_codex/ids/candidates.py:120`) and its post-hoc filter (`imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:681–694`); no other mapping-pipeline mechanism retrieves DD nodes for the map stage. `imas_codex/ids/tools.py` is already in §8's `map-run-consumes-candidates` write paths

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py` becomes the one deep module for both edge families (MAPS_TO_IMAS write + delete, MAPPING_CANDIDATE write + clear + read + select + count), so §8 concentrates surface rather than spreading it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §8 relies on `compute_semantic_matches` as the per-source wiki/code bridge while that function still owns its own IMAS-node retrieval arm, duplicating the DD retrieval that `retrieve_candidates` owns.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §8 adds no new CLI option (the shortlist size is the existing `map-shortlist-size` setting in `imas_codex/settings.py:1104`) and names what it retires or merges (`--skip-metadata`, `--skip-errors`, `mapping_target_path`/`mapping_target_ids`, `count_sources_by_mapping_status`, `create_signal_source`), so it accounts for its surface in its own text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §8 cites prior art by exact file:line (the three `MERGE (sg)-[r|rel:MAPS_TO_IMAS]` writers, the single delete, `create_signal_source`'s only caller) and its two census greps reproduce exactly (`grep -rnE 'MERGE \(sg\)-\[(r|rel):MAPS_TO_IMAS\]' imas_codex/` → models.py:580, mapping.py:2008, graph_ops.py:367; the delete grep → cli/map.py:661), and it reuses `claims.py` claim routines, `compute_semantic_matches`, `fetch_cross_facility_mappings` and `retrieve_candidates` rather than rebuilding them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one wrapper-shaped addition, `select_candidate` beside `write_candidates`, carries an explicit justification for why the existing writer cannot be extended (`write_candidates` deletes and rewrites every edge; a pick must flag one existing edge), which is the justification the item requires.
